recent_posts.title: Validate user input, don't sanitize it
recent_posts.summary: A strong argument against the common advice to 'sanitize user input', explaining the important distinction between sanitization and validation. Sanitization modifies data based on assumed intent, risking data loss and misinterpretation, while validation checks that input meets defined requirements without altering it. The correct approach is to validate input, reject non-conforming data, use prepared statements to prevent SQL injection, and encode/escape data at the point of use — not at the point of storage. Client-side validation is also insufficient for security since it can always be bypassed.

recent_posts.title: Dinit, the init system systemd should have been
recent_posts.summary: A critical look at systemd's scope creep and an endorsement of Dinit as a leaner alternative. Dinit is a portable, dependency-based service manager and init system written in C++ that runs on Linux and BSDs. Unlike systemd, it is designed to work alongside other system components rather than replace them, follows Unix philosophy, and offers a smaller attack surface. The author recommends trying Dinit via Artix Linux and expresses hope that major distributions will adopt it as a systemd alternative.

recent_posts.title: The reasons for the big discrepancy between satisfied vs dissatisfied developers using AI for coding
recent_posts.summary: Developers have vastly different opinions on AI coding tools based on their experience level and approach. Amateur developers love AI because it produces seemingly working code quickly, but they often miss hidden bugs and security issues while stalling their learning process. Lazy experienced developers appreciate AI as a time-saver and can fix its mistakes. Artisan programmers who value craftsmanship generally dislike AI, finding that fixing AI-generated code takes longer than writing quality code from scratch. Environmental concerns about AI datacenters further divide opinions between those who overlook these issues and those who see them as unjustified given AI's output quality.

recent_posts.title: How to change the init system in Artix Linux to Dinit
recent_posts.summary: Dinit is a lightweight, POSIX-compatible init system written in C++ that offers dependency management and service supervision without the complexity of systemd. This guide walks through migrating Artix Linux from OpenRC or runit to Dinit by saving current services, downloading Dinit packages, uninstalling old init files, installing new ones, and enabling services using the --offline flag with dinitctl. The process requires working from the console and uses Linux Magic SysRq keys for rebooting since normal reboot commands won't work during the transition.

recent_posts.title: Why AI coding tools provide limited value for software development
recent_posts.summary: A critical perspective on AI coding tools argues they provide limited value (15-20% productivity) and often produce poor quality code. The author contends AI has reached its technological peak due to fundamental mathematical limitations, citing studies showing experienced developers take 19% longer when using AI tools. The piece advocates for treating AI as extended search rather than a primary development tool, emphasizing that genuine programming skill development requires traditional research, experimentation, and critical thinking.

recent_posts.title: How I manage my bookmarks
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their custom bookmark management system using local HTML files stored in a Git repository. The approach involves creating categorized HTML files in a hidden folder, adding them to browser toolbars via file URLs, and syncing across devices using Git. This method intentionally adds friction to prevent casual bookmarking while maintaining simplicity and avoiding cloud dependencies or browser extensions.

recent_posts.title: Rethinking GitHub for open source projects
recent_posts.summary: The post criticizes GitHub for its proprietary nature, centralized model, and involvement with Microsoft, highlighting concerns over privacy, user control, and political associations. It suggests alternative platforms like Forgejo, Sourcehut, and Codeberg for hosting open source projects, emphasizing a decentralized and open-source approach. Additionally, it raises concerns about Microsoft's contracts with government entities and its technology's use in conflicts, prompting calls for change from within the company.

recent_posts.title: Evilness is when profit is the sole concern
recent_posts.summary: As companies grow, prioritizing profit over ethical values can lead to compromising principles, often seen in large tech corporations. The post discusses how initial passionate ideas can be overshadowed by investor-driven profit motives, using Google as an example of becoming more commercialized over time. It emphasizes the importance of consumer choices and encourages individuals to reflect on their decisions' impact and strive for conscientious choices.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft CEO says up to 30% of the company's code is written by AI - no surprise there
recent_posts.summary: Microsoft's CEO states that up to 30% of the company's code is created by AI, sparking concerns about the quality and implications of AI-written code in the tech industry. The author expresses skepticism about this trend, suggesting it is driven by corporate greed and criticizing the industry's declining standards.

recent_posts.title: Hypocrisy and politics in free and open source software projects
recent_posts.summary: Kim McMahon's presentation at EuroBSDCon 2024 reveals contradictions in her advocacy for FreeBSD, raising concerns about big tech's influence on open source projects. The post examines the roles big companies play in foundations like FreeBSD and Linux, and critiques their dominating presence in the FOSS community.

top_posts.title: There is only one reason why Microsoft Windows is the dominating operating system on the PC desktop
top_posts.summary: Microsoft Windows dominates the PC desktop market primarily because it is the default operating system installed on most new desktops and laptops. This long-standing practice has led many consumers to equate PCs with Windows, unaware of other operating systems like Linux. Challenges with Linux often stem from user habits formed around Windows, hardware and software vendor lock-in, and selecting less-supported Linux distributions.
